COSL says parent CNOOC bought 405,000 A shares on the market, adding to its controlling stake in the offshore drilling and services contractor serving Bohai Bay and South China Sea fields.

China Oilfield Services Limited (COSL) disclosed that its parent company, China National Offshore Oil Corporation (CNOOC), increased its shareholding in the company by 405,000 A shares.
CNOOC conducted the purchase on the open market, according to the company's statement. The acquisition adds to CNOOC's already controlling position in the Shanghai- and Hong Kong-listed oilfield services provider, which operates the drilling rig fleet, well services, and geophysical survey units serving CNOOC's offshore E&P program in Bohai Bay and the South China Sea.

candidates.title: ABRAJ Energy Services Awarded $312 million Hydraulic Fracturing Contract with PDO - SaudiGulf Projects
candidates.source_name: ABRAJ Energy Services Awarded $312 million Hydraulic Fracturing Contract with PDO - SaudiGulf Projects
candidates.snippet:
ABRAJ Energy Services, Oman’s leading drilling and oilfield services provider​, announced that it has secured a major hydraulic fracturing (“frac”) contract with Petroleum Development Oman (“PDO”).
The new contract represents a direct continuation and an upgrade of ABRAJ’s existing frac services agreement with PDO and is expected to commence in the second quarter of 2026.
The contract has a five‑year duration and an estimated value of approximately OMR 120 million , which will be added to the Company’s overall backlog.
Under the upgraded scope of work, the contract includes the deployment of one additional frac fleet and covers more complex, high‑end operations, including gas well fracturing services.
